result.rationale: In deleteEvent the diff shows `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When externalCalendarId is falsy, the find compares each cal.externalId against the falsy externalCalendarId (undefined/null), so it never matches and calendarId is undefined; the pre-diff code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same contradictory pattern appears in updateEvent's `selectedCalendar`. Passing undefined as calendarId to calendar.events.delete means the event is not deleted

judged_text: deleteEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and calendarId resolves to undefined where the old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined — the Google event is never removed and remains as an orphan on the host's calendar after the booking is cancelled in Cal.com.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now sets `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), it searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy `externalCalendarId`, which will typically return `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single DC). With the new array type, this logic can produce `calendarId` undefined and pass it into `calendar.events.delete`, breaking deletion. The same flawed pattern also appears in `updateEvent`.
